description: Emergency POCUS interpretation corpus for the Clinical Reasoning Agent.
licence_note: Store a citation and a short quotation per passage. Do NOT redistribute whole guideline documents: most are copyrighted. Every passage must name where its text came from before the corpus is used for anything reported.
how_to_use: Replace each entry whose status is 'placeholder' with real text and a real citation, then set status to 'sourced'. Retrieval returns placeholders so the pipeline is testable, but reason() marks any answer resting on them as NOT guideline-grounded, so a placeholder can never be mistaken for evidence.

passages.source: REPLACE: citation for what B-lines indicate
passages.text: B-lines: what their presence indicates, how many are needed to be significant, and which conditions they support.

passages.source: REPLACE: citation for B-lines and pneumothorax
passages.text: B-lines and pneumothorax: why the presence of B-lines argues against pneumothorax at the site examined.
A-lines: what they represent and what they do and do not exclude.
Consolidation on lung ultrasound: appearance, what it supports, and what its absence does not exclude.

passages.source: REPLACE: citation for pleural effusion on ultrasound
passages.text: Pleural effusion: appearance, associated conditions, and the limits of a negative examination.
Pleural thickening: what it indicates, and which acute conditions it does NOT bear on. Written explicitly because the reasoning model cited its absence as evidence against pulmonary embolism.

passages.source: REPLACE: Lichtenstein and Meziere, Chest 2008 — quote the relevant decision point
passages.text: BLUE protocol: the decision points linking lung ultrasound profiles to the principal causes of acute respiratory failure.

passages.source: REPLACE: citation for focused echocardiography in shock
passages.text: Focused echocardiography: what a focused study assesses in undifferentiated shock, and what it cannot exclude.

passages.source: REPLACE: citation for the FAST examination
passages.text: FAST: the windows examined, what free fluid indicates, and the sensitivity limits of a negative study.

Troponin: the reference threshold, what a value below it means, and why a single normal value early after symptom onset does not exclude myocardial injury. Included deliberately as a test: the model called a normal troponin 'elevated' in every pre-RAG run, with the reference range already in front of it. If retrieval does not fix that, it is evidence that the failure is inattention rather than missing knowledge.
